The Full Scan Report page (screenshot) clearly states this is a simulated demo and warns that the Identity Exposure Check is a data-extraction trap — submitting sensitive data (SSN) to this unknown site is unsafe. I closed the report and will not submit any further personal or financial information to this site. Recommended next steps for you:

- Treat the SSN that was entered here as potentially exposed. Consider placing a fraud alert and/or credit freeze with the major US credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion) immediately.
- Monitor your bank and credit-card accounts closely for unauthorized activity. Consider enabling alerts and changing passwords for financial accounts.
- Consider ordering a credit report and identity monitoring service from a reputable vendor, or use free annualcreditreport.com for the official reports.
- If you reused passwords or credentials on other sites, change those passwords now and enable multi-factor authentication where available.
- If you believe the SSN or other data has been misused, file a report with the FTC (identitytheft.gov) and consider filing a police report.
- For real system scans use reputable antivirus/antimalware tools downloaded directly from vendor sites (e.g., Microsoft Defender, Malwarebytes) rather than unknown web-based scanners.

I did not submit any additional sensitive information to the site and followed the PHISHING CHECKLIST: the domain looked like a local demo and the report confirms it is a simulation and a trap, so no further submission is appropriate.
